note:
**The 1881 round, schedules 75 to 98 - Derby Terrace, Western Terrace, North Road, Barrack Lane and Pelham Crescent.** Transcribed by A. Hagues as the images came in. The piece is **RG11/3367**.

**Three of the 1871 placements come from these pages**, and each rests on every age advancing by ten rather than on a surname:

- **Thomas Mann at 14 Pelham Crescent.** The 1871 round had him at "The Park", an engine fitter of 34 among labourers, and the household looked too modest for the Crescent. It is the same man: at 44 he is a box maker employing seventeen, his wife, son and daughter all advance exactly ten years, and Agnes is born at Sheffield in both rounds. **The doubt was mine and it was wrong.**
- **John and Ann Loverseed at 16 Pelham Crescent**, the contractor and builder of 1871, now retired.
- **James B Alliott at 1 Western Terrace** - a colonial and civil engineer of 26 living with his mother in 1871, head of the house at 36 and a master employing 328 men and 54 boys.

**Schedule 75 is the Chief Constable, and it is not Derby House.** The household is **William Henry Poyntz, 42, "Major, Royal Marines, retired" and Chief Constable of Nottingham**, born Dublin, with six children born at Chatham, Cork, Friern Barnet, Nottingham and New Radford - a career written in birthplaces. The page numbers the house **159** and appears also to name it Derby House. **The record holds 159 Derby Road as 2 Derby Terrace, and Derby House separately as 1 Derby Terrace**, so the two cannot both be right. The household is filed on the number, which is the harder evidence, and the house name is recorded in the source line as the doubtful part. See [[derby-house-is-not-159-derby-road]].

**Western Terrace is numbered - 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9 - and the school is not.** **Western House**, Louisa Clark's girls' boarding school, carries a name and no number, so it is unfiled. It is the fourth girls' school in this district in one round, and its staff come from Manchester, Oldenburg and Kentish Town.

**Pelham Crescent is barely numbered at all on these pages.** Only 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 carry a figure; schedules 88, 89, 93, 94 and 95 say "Pelham Crescent" and nothing more. Among the unnumbered is **John Henry Brown, wine merchant, with seven children** - the same household whose 1891 number the record could not settle. **1881 does not settle it either**, but it confirms the family was on the Crescent ten years earlier than the disputed page.

**Schedule 92 is deliberately left out.** Fletcher Hind's household at Pelham Cottage is already in the record from the earlier Pelham Crescent transcription, at the same schedule number, and matches line for line - which is a useful check that these two readings of the same book agree.

**One entry could not be read.** Schedule 94's occupation column is overwritten and illegible, so Charles Sidney Hill is entered with none.

**Readings that could go either way are flagged in the source line.** Infants are entered as age 0 with the real age kept in the source.

**A surname corrected after the fact.** I read the household at 10 Barrack Lane as **Perry**. A. Hagues read the page again: it is **Derry** - and the same George Derry heads the house in 1901 and 1911, born Bingham both times, which is what the 1881 page says too. Lizzie's occupation, "Groom's wife", was blank in my reading and is restored.
source: 1881 census enumerator's book, Standard Hill and Limits of the Castle of Nottingham, schedules 75 to 98, transcribed by A. Hagues.
